en: The Sūtra on the Dharma Gate of the Boundless Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha, translated by the Śramaṇa Shengjian of the Western Qin.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of twelve hundred and fifty bhikṣus and twelve thousand bodhisattvas,
all of whom were in their final birth before attaining enlightenment and were worthy of the position of a venerable one.
They have all come from the worlds of the ten directions to this assembly;
they have all attained dhāraṇīs and unimpeded eloquence,
their resolve is firm and steadfast, and what they speak is the ultimate truth.
The precious and reverent Dharma of non-negligence is their [attire],
with shame, remorse, loving-kindness, and patience as their upper garments;
they have attained unimpeded mastery over the wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas.
They are able to act as friends to sentient beings;
out of compassion for all, they skillfully guide and transform them,
enabling sentient beings to draw near to them with reverence and affection.
They travel unhindered through the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions by means of their supernormal powers;
they are able to comprehend the faculties of all sentient beings,
subdue all desires, and tear asunder the net of Māra.
Having already transcended the realm of Māra and abandoned all habitual tendencies toward desire,
they are fully able to encompass the nature of all phenomena and reverently practice the Dharma in accordance with the teachings of all Buddhas.
All that he contemplates consists entirely of various meditative concentrations (*dhyāna-samādhi*).
Whether sitting, rising, walking, or standing, he never loses his dignified deportment (*īryāpatha*).
His name is Bodhisattva Drum of Infinite Resonance.
The Bodhisattva Endless Banner,
the Bodhisattva Endless Praise,
and the Bodhisattva Endless Name.
Bodhisattva King of Trees,
Bodhisattva Knower of All Sounds,
and Bodhisattva Banner of Renown.
The Bodhisattva Sarvavyūpadhvaja [received it] from the Bodhisattva Anantadhvaja and the Bodhisattva Samantamati.
The Bodhisattva Universal Renown,
the Bodhisattva Universal Radiance,
and the Bodhisattva Universal Designation.
The Bodhisattva Universal Banner,
the Bodhisattva All-Pervasive Arrival,
and the Bodhisattva Sovereign King of Universal Virtue Banners.
The Bodhisattva Proclaiming Renown,
the Bodhisattva Gathering Renown,
and the Bodhisattva Gathering Excellence.
The Bodhisattva Universal Eye;
the Bodhisattva Universal Virtue;
the Bodhisattva Seeing No Deficiency.
Bodhisattvas free from deficiency;
bodhisattvas who have already become free from deficiency;
bodhisattvas who fulfill the aspirations of all sentient beings.
The Bodhisattva who does not abandon any sentient being;
the Bodhisattva who is ever-concerned with their welfare;
the Bodhisattva who has accomplished the most supreme state.
The Bodhisattva Sarvaguṇanāman was the leader of those twelve thousand bodhisattvas,
all of whom were such foremost ones as he.
At that time, the Heavenly King Yama arrived with sixty billion celestial sons of the Yama realm and sat together in the assembly.
The Heavenly King Tuṣita arrived with eight billion devas and sat together in the assembly.
The King of the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations (Nirmāṇarati) arrived with ninety-two nayuta-hundred-thousand devas to join the assembly.
The King of the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Emanations (Paranirmita-vaśavartin) arrived with fifty-five thousand nayutas of devas to join the assembly.
Countless devas from the realm of form came together and sat in assembly.
At that time, to the east of this Sahā world-system,
beyond worlds as numerous as the atoms in ninety-two buddha-fields, [there was...]
There is a land named Mahābala.
In that land there is a Buddha named Saṃghamahābalas tathāgata, arhat, samyaksaṃbuddha.
There is a venerable bodhisattva named Sūryavijitāri.
Together with countless hundreds of thousands of millions of bodhisattvas,
they suddenly vanished from that buddha-field and arrived in this Sahā world.
In the void above this trichiliocosm,
he stood and raised clouds of lapis lazuli that covered the world everywhere,
raining down flowers of Jambūnada gold.
Throughout the entire Sahā world,
each and every bodhisattva further rained down various exquisite necklaces made of the seven treasures,
as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field.
Each and every bodhisattva further rained down celestial mandārava flowers,
as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field;
each and every bodhisattva further rained down various kinds of celestial incense.
As numerous as the atoms in a single buddha-field,
each and every bodhisattva likewise rained down celestial agalloch incense,
as numerous as the atoms in a single buddha-field.
Each and every bodhisattva further rained down seven-jeweled whisks and ornaments,
as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field;
each and every bodhisattva further rained down celestial sandalwood incense.
As numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field,
each and every bodhisattva likewise rained down garments of various colors,
equal in number to the atoms within a single buddha-field.
Each and every bodhisattva further rained down various wonderful jeweled canopies,
as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field;
each and every bodhisattva further rained down exquisite, multicolored jeweled canopies.
As numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field,
each and every bodhisattva likewise rained down beryl jewel canopies,
as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field.
Each and every bodhisattva further rained down canopies of red pearls,
as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field;
each and every bodhisattva further rained down canopies of fine lapis lazuli.
As many as there are atoms in a single buddha-field,
each and every bodhisattva likewise rained down coral jewel-canopies,
as numerous as the atoms in a single buddha-field.
Each and every bodhisattva further rained down banners made of various precious jewels,
as numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field.
Each and every bodhisattva further [uttered] subtle and unprecedented verses.
As numerous as the atoms within a single buddha-field,
they extolled and praised the World-Honored One, the Able One (Śākyamuni).
At that time, throughout the trichiliocosm...
The agonies of all the hells were entirely stilled;
among animals, there was a heart of compassion such that they did not devour one another;
and the hungry ghosts were at peace, free from any thought of hunger or thirst.
The afflictions of all people— greed, hatred, and delusion— were entirely stilled. Furthermore,
there was no suffering of hunger, thirst, cold, or heat,
nor any distress from day or night, wind, or dust.
Their minds were tranquil, free from deluded thoughts;
there was no longer form, sound, fragrance, flavor, touch, or mental afflictions.
The confusion and distracted minds of the various devas in the desire realm were entirely stilled.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Jayanta stood upon the Akaniṣṭha Heaven and offered remote worship to the Tathāgata Śākyamuni with various kinds of exquisite mixed flowers,
ground incense, liquid perfumes, multicolored fine garments, parasols, banners, pennants, and various precious necklaces.
It rained everywhere throughout the trichiliocosm.
Furthermore, it rained upon all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and all other devas and nāgas, as well as throughout the four continents.
It pervaded the entire trichiliocosm,
with rare and wondrous jewels filling it everywhere.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Jayavīra...
Descending from above,
he first approached the Buddha’s dwelling, prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, and circumambulated him a hundred thousand times.
He then offered robes inlaid with *maṇi* jewels, *vajra*, and various exquisite gems.
Having presented these offerings to the Buddha,
he sat to one side. Then,
the Bodhisattva Jayadatta [examined] each and every meaning of the Dharma.
Universally observing the spheres of dharma entered by all Buddhas of the three periods of time,
one grasps every eloquence within the teachings of the Buddhas—
namely, unceasing eloquence.
The eloquence of union;
the eloquence of penetration;
the unimpeded eloquence.
The dialectic of extreme proximity;
the dialectic of infinity;
the dialectic of ease of understanding.
The eloquence of being fully endowed;
the eloquence of skillfully expounding the nature of all phenomena through spontaneous speech;
and the eloquence of analytically expounding nirvana through emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness.
The eloquence that distinguishes all meditative concentrations perfumed by various volitions and discerns all liberations;
the eloquence that analyzes the underlying intent and expounds upon it;
and the eloquence that swiftly abandons verbal discourse through diligent exertion.
He has attained the eloquence of moving, sitting, and rising with supernormal powers;
he possesses the eloquence of discourse regarding all manifest consciousnesses— superior, middling, and inferior—
and his eloquence of verbal expression is such that none can subdue it.
He sought eloquence regarding the seven factors of enlightenment and the noble eightfold path;
he expounded the eloquence of meditative wisdom that is neither high nor low;
and he was well able to distinguish the eloquence of the Dharma and Vinaya.
Such eloquence of truthful and authentic speech is like an illusion,
like a magical transformation, like a mirage in the heat of the sun,
and like the moon reflected in water.
Like an echo following a call,
like a reflection in a mirror—
thus he expounds that the nature of all phenomena is entirely such.
The discourse on non-arising, non-origination, and non-extinction;
the most refined and subtle discourse;
the most profound and wondrous discourse.
The analysis of mixed types;
the analysis of extreme distances;
and the analysis of various desires.
He possesses the eloquence that distinguishes the mentalities and desires of all sentient beings to lead them toward the supreme state;
he possesses the eloquence that brings compassion for the cycle of sentient beings like thunder and rain filling the world.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vijayavikrama understood the power of eloquence taught by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
He immediately rose from his seat, adjusted his robes,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms,
and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Indeed, World-Honored One,
I wish to ask a question.
If the Tathāgata permits it, I shall venture to ask."
The World-Honored One said:
"Ask whatever you wish;
I shall explain it to you in full detail."
Having received the Buddha’s permission,
the Bodhisattva Jayavijaya leaped for joy and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How is this so, World-Honored One?"
How could all phenomena have a beginning, an end, a root, a source, a name, or a characteristic that can be apprehended?
Yet, they are still spoken of.
Regarding the various dhyāna-concentrations of the bodhisattvas and the places where they enter them:
They possess mastery over speech such that they can answer whatever is asked;
though they have a standard of reference, their words are free from error, yet they do not perceive any such standard.
Furthermore, they transform sentient beings so that they may attain this same Dharma.
All eloquence is fully accomplished;
as for those who have attained dhāraṇī,
it is said that they have attained that which is boundless.
By means of this dhāraṇī, one attains boundless and subtle eloquence,
universally upholding all that has been spoken by the Buddhas,
and gains the gate of boundless dhāraṇīs.
Universally upholding the Dharma-realm, they fully know its points of entry;
they have ultimately and thoroughly realized the subtle and wondrous nature of phenomena,
and clearly understand all sense-bases.
He clearly understands entry into the five destinies;
he clearly understands the Four Noble Truths;
he clearly understands entry into the various phenomena of dependent origination.
They clearly understand the habitual tendencies of sentient beings;
they clearly understand all phenomena as being characterized by ignorance;
and they clearly enter into the absence of intrinsic nature.
One clearly understands and perceives the existence of the notion of self;
one clearly understands and enters into the notion of non-self;
one clearly understands and enters into emptiness.
He clearly understands and enters into the nature of non-emptiness;
he clearly understands and enters into manifest consciousness;
and he clearly understands and enters into non-manifest consciousness.
He clearly enters into aspiration;
he clearly enters into wishlessness.
He has clarity regarding the self and clarity regarding the non-self.
He is clear regarding that which has a basis and clear regarding that which is without a basis;
he is clear regarding that which arises and clear regarding that which does not arise.
In every place and in all verbal expressions, [he is thus clear].
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Jayamitra, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Jayamitra!"
That a bodhisattva is able to feel compassion for all sentient beings and inquire about such a matter as this from the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha—
listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well.
"I shall now explain this to you in full detail and distinction.
Bodhisattva Jayavijaya, together with the great assembly,
should listen with single-minded attention and a tranquil mind, receiving these instructions."
The Buddha told Jayanta:
"What is meant by this name 'Entry into the Boundless,' which encompasses all dharmas?"
Because of this dhāraṇī, one attains unsurpassed renown;
with this unsurpassed renown as one's retinue, one proceeds.
The Dharma-gate of Infinite Virtue,
which takes infinite virtue as its retinue;
the Dharma-gate of Stainless Purity.
Taking stainlessness as its wing and retinue,
it is the dharma-gate of tranquility;
taking tranquility as its wing and retinue.
Swiftly follow the Dharma-gate;
take swift following as your winged companion;
swiftly proclaim the Dharma-gate.
Taking joy as one's followers, one takes the Dharma-gate of joy as one's followers.
Taking compassion as one's followers, one takes the Dharma-gate of compassion as one's followers.
The Dharma-gate of the Auspicious Image,
taking the auspicious image as its retinue;
the Dharma-gate of Immovability.
Taking immovability as one's retinue,
one accomplishes the dharma-gate;
taking accomplishment as one's retinue, one [proceeds].
The Dharma-door of Thorough Realization through Self-Perfection;
taking thorough realization through self-perfection as its attendant;
the Dharma-door of Non-Categorical Equality.
Taking the "No-Category" as its retinue is like the Flower Dharma-gate;
taking the "Metaphorical Flower" as its retinue is likewise so.
The Dharma-gate of skillful conformity;
taking skillful conformity as one's winged companion,
it is the Dharma-gate of non-wandering.
Taking non-wandering as one's retinue;
taking the dharma-gate of non-concealment as one's retinue by means of non-concealment.
The Dharma-gate of Entering Concealment,
with entering concealment as its attendant;
the Dharma-gate of Contentment.
Taking contentment as its wing-follower,
it is the Dharma-gate of skillful treading;
taking skillful treading as its wing-follower.
The dharma-gate of relinquishment,
with relinquishment as its wing and follower;
the dharma-gate of being without evil.
Taking the absence of evil as its retinue is the Dharma-gate of Universal Radiance;
taking universal radiance as its retinue [is the Dharma-gate of the Absence of Evil].
The Dharma-gate of Roaming the Boundless Limits takes roaming the boundless limits as its retinue;
the Dharma-gate of Generating Vitality takes generating vitality as its retinue.
They roam the gateway of stainlessness,
taking roaming in stainlessness as their winged attendants;
they are the gateway of firmness.
With steadfastness as its wing and following,
it is the dharma-gate of non-deceit;
with non-deceit as its wing and following, it proceeds.
Revere this Dharma-gate;
with reverence as your winged companion,
travel through the most profound and eternal Dharma-gate.
Taking the far-reaching journey as one's retinue;
taking the dharma-gate of mental sufficiency as one's retinue, with mental sufficiency itself serving as the retinue.
The Dharma-gate of detachment from birth,
with detachment from birth as its wing and follower;
the Dharma-gate of lightness and elevation.
Taking lightness and elevation as its wings and followers is the Dharma-gate of non-doubt;
taking non-doubt as its wings and followers is [the Dharma-gate of]... [non-doubt].
The Dharma-gate of Eliminating Boundless Suffering,
which takes the elimination of boundless suffering as its auxiliary;
and the Dharma-gate of Severing the Nest.
Taking the severance of the nest as one's retinue;
taking the dharma-gate of departing from the ultimate nest as one's retinue;
taking the departure from the ultimate nest as one's retinue.
The delightful dharma-gate,
with delight as its winged retinue;
the dharma-gate of gentle nature and joy.
Taking the pleasure of gentleness as its winged attendant;
taking the non-perverted dharma-gate as its winged attendant by means of non-perversion.
The Dharma-gate of Fearlessness,
which takes fearlessness as its retinue;
the Dharma-gate of Skillfulness Surpassing All.
Taking skill that surpasses others as its attendant,
it is the dharma-door of non-forgetfulness and non-alarm;
taking non-forgetfulness and non-alarm as its attendant.
The Dharma-gate of Rootlessness,
which takes rootlessness as its winged attendants;
the Dharma-gate of Skillful Victory.
Taking "excellence through goodness" as one's winged attendants;
taking the "Dharma-gate of non-apprehension" as one's winged attendants,
with "non-apprehension" itself serving as the winged attendants.
The Dharma-gate of a Single Matter,
which takes a single matter as its attendant;
the Dharma-gate of Delighting in Accumulation.
Taking the accumulation of what is pleasant as their retinue,
they diminish the gates of the Dharma;
taking this diminution as their retinue, they proceed.
The Dharma-gate of Non-action,
with non-action as its wing and follower;
the Dharma-gate of Ceasing Thought.
Taking the cessation of non-thought as one's attendants leads to the dharma-gate of "having nowhere to which one goes.
Taking this state of having nowhere to which one goes as one's attendants [leads to liberation].
The Dharma-gate of No Coming takes no coming as its attendant;
the Dharma-gate of No Face takes no face as its attendant.
The Dharma-gate of Majestic Power,
which takes majestic power as its retinue;
the Dharma-gate that is upheld.
That which is maintained serves as its winged retinue;
the Dharma-gate of the pure mind takes the pure mind as its winged retinue.
The Dharma-gate of Welcome,
which takes welcome as its attendant;
the Dharma-gate of the Step Without Intent.
Taking the state of no-thought as one's retinue;
taking the Dharma-meaning and the Dharma-gate as one's retinue;
taking the Dharma-meaning itself as one's retinue.
The Dharma-gate of Non-Cultivation,
taking non-cultivation as its retinue;
the Dharma-gate of Fearlessness.
Taking fearlessness as one's retinue;
the dharma-gate of the mental faculty of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā),
taking the mental faculty of the nature of phenomena as one's retinue.
The Dharma-gate of the Tathāgata’s Intention:
taking the Tathāgata’s intention as one's winged followers,
it proclaims the Dharma-gate of the Intention.
Taking the intent of proclaiming [the Dharma] as one's retinue;
taking the dharma-gate of being without sleep as one's retinue, with non-sleep as the retinue.
The Dharma-gate of Celestial Intent,
which takes celestial intent as its winged attendants;
the Dharma-gate of Dragon Intent.
Taking the mind of a nāga as their retinue,
they have the dharma-gate of the yakṣa-mind;
taking the mind of a yakṣa as their retinue.
The Dharma-gate of the Gandharva-mind,
taking the Gandharva-mind as its retinue;
the Dharma-gate of the Asura-mind.
The gateway of the garuḍas has the asuras as its followers;
the gateway of the kiṃnaras has the garuḍas as its followers.
With the kiṃnaras as their retinue,
they employ the dharmaparyāya of the mahoragas;
with the mahoragas as their retinue, they [employ it].
The Dharma-gate of the Great Dragon’s Mind,
which takes the mind of the Great Dragon as its winged retinue;
the Dharma-gate of the Human Mind.
Taking human intention as one's wing and follower is not the dharma-gate of non-human intention;
taking non-human intention as one's wing and follower is [the dharma-gate].
The Dharma-gate of Moon-Mind,
with Moon-Mind as its attendant;
the Dharma-gate of Sun-Mind.
Taking the solar intention as its winged retinue,
it is the dharma-gate of the stellar intention;
taking the stellar intention as its winged retinue.
The Dharma-door of the Space-like Mind,
which takes the space-like mind as its attendant;
the Dharma-door of the Unobstructed Mind.
Taking unimpeded mental engagement as one's winged attendants,
one enters the Dharma-gate of Dispelling Doubt;
taking the dispelling of doubt as one's winged attendants.
The gateway of following through doubt:
taking following through doubt as one's winged attendant,
one brings forth the gateway of the mental faculty.
Taking the intention as one's wing and follower,
one uses the "Excellently Renowned" Dharma-gate;
taking the "Excellently Renowned" as one's wing and follower.
The Dharma-door of Jewel-Mind,
with Jewel-Mind as its retinue;
the Dharma-door of Freedom from Sorrow.
Taking the departure from sorrow as one's winged retinue,
one increases the dharma-gates;
taking this increase as one's winged retinue.
The Dharma-gate of Detachment from Craving,
which takes detachment from craving as its attendant;
the Dharma-gate of Severing the Net of Destruction.
With the "Net of Severing Destruction" as its retinue,
it is the Dharma-gate of Swift Arrival;
with "Swift Arrival" as its retinue.
The Dharma-gate of Thoroughly Examining and Pairing;
taking thorough examination and pairing as one's winged attendants;
the Dharma-gate of Leaving the Nest of Pleasure.
Taking the departure from the nest of pleasure as their retinue;
taking the dharma-gate of non-retrogression as their retinue, with non-retrogression as their retinue.
The Dharma-door of Detachment from Beauty,
with detachment from beauty as its attendant;
the Dharma-door of the Virtue of Seeking a Good Name.
One takes a good reputation and virtue as one's followers;
the Dharma naturally follows from the gate of wholesome dharmas,
and thus one takes the Dharma’s own wholesomeness as one's followers.
The Dharma-gate of Swift Course,
taking swift course as its winged retinue;
the Dharma-gate of Non-deception.
Taking freedom from hypocrisy as one's retinue;
the dharma-gate of departing from the evil realms,
taking departure from the evil realms as one's retinue.
The Dharma-gate of Great Majesty,
which takes great majesty as its retinue;
the Dharma-gate of Transcending Vows.
Taking detachment from aspiration as one's retinue;
taking the dharma-gate of being unstained like a lotus flower as one's retinue.
Taking being unstained like a lotus flower as one's retinue.
The Dharma-gate of Boundless Joy,
which takes boundless joy as its attendant;
the Dharma-gate of Taming the Mind.
Taking the subduing of the mind as its retinue is the Dharma-gate of the Great Hero’s Marks;
taking the marks of the Great Hero as its retinue [is the Dharma-gate of the Subduing of the Mind].
The Dharma-gate of Detachment from Enumeration,
taking detachment from enumeration as its retinue;
the Dharma-gate of Detachment from Weeding.
Taking the abandonment of weeding as one's retinue,
one lightly contemplates the Dharma-gate;
taking this light contemplation as one's retinue.
The Dharma-gate of Spontaneous Union,
taking spontaneous union as its retinue;
the Dharma-gate of the Gold Practice.
Taking the golden wheel as its retinue,
it has the various jewel dharma-gates;
taking the various jewels as its retinue.
The Dharma-door of Abandoning Harmfulness,
which takes the abandonment of harmfulness as its retinue;
the Dharma-door of Vastness Without Limit.
Taking the vastness that has no boundaries as their retinue;
taking the majesty and spiritual power that accords with the Dharma-gate as their retinue. Taking the majesty and spiritual power that accords with the Dharma-gate as their retinue.
The Dharma-gate of Vast Intention,
with vast intention as its attendant;
the Dharma-gate of Expansiveness.
The Dharma-door of Vastness has vastness as its retinue;
the Dharma-door of the Great Sound has the great sound as its retinue;
[and] the Dharma-door of Departing from the Dusts of the Great Realm.
Taking the departure from the dust of the great realm as one’s retinue;
taking the knowledge of the appropriate timing for the Dharma-gate as one’s retinue.
The Dharma-gate of Separation from Time takes separation from time as its attendant;
it is like the Sword Dharma-gate.
With the sword as its wing and attendant,
it proceeds toward the dharma-gate of contentment;
with the proceeding toward contentment as its wing and attendant, it proceeds further.
The Dharma-gate of Wandering Perfumed by Fragrance takes wandering perfumed by fragrance as its retinue;
it is the Dharma-gate of Knowing Numbers.
Taking the knowledge of numbers as one's retinue,
one enters the dharma-gate of non-deficiency;
taking entry into non-deficiency as one's retinue.
The Dharma-gate of Universal Roaming,
taking universal roaming as its attendant;
the Dharma-gate of Freedom from Affliction.
Taking the absence of afflictions as one's retinue,
one roams through the dharma-gate of self-discipline;
taking this roaming through self-discipline as one's retinue.
The Dharma-gate of Practice and Subsequent Detachment;
with practice and subsequent detachment as its attendants,
it wanders through the Dharma-gate of the Hidden Treasury.
Taking the "wandering, concealing, and hiding" as its attendants,
it is the dharma-gate of the "wandering shadow";
taking the "wandering shadow" as its attendants.
Having already crossed over by means of the dharma-gate of having already crossed over, one enters the dharma-gate of freedom from defilement with that very crossing as one's winged companion.
Taking entry into freedom from defilement as one's retinue is the dharma-gate of pure conduct;
taking pure conduct as one's retinue is the dharma-gate of pure conduct.
The Dharma-gate of Compassionate Pacing,
which takes compassionate pacing as its retinue;
the Dharma-gate of Departing from Turbidity.
Taking the departure from turbidity as its attendants;
the Dharma-gate of abandoning doubt,
taking the abandonment of doubt as its attendants.
He delights in the gateway of the joyful image,
taking the joyful image as his retinue;
he resembles the gateway of the true Dharma.
Taking the semblance as its retinue,
it has the gate of prostration as its retinue;
taking prostration as its retinue, [it proceeds].
The Dharma-gate of Tāranirghoṣa,
with Tāranirghoṣa as its retinue;
the Dharma-gate of Wandering in the Purity of Space.
Taking the purity of roaming through space as one's retinue,
one enters the most excellent Dharma-gate;
taking this entry into the most excellent as one's retinue.
One traverses the gateway of lofty wandering,
taking lofty wandering as one's winged attendants,
and proceeds toward the gateway of dharma-friends.
Taking the pursuit of friends as one's winged retinue;
taking the King’s Gait Dharma-gate as one's winged retinue.
The Dharma-gate of the Objective Sphere takes the objective sphere as its wings and attendants,
just like the Dharma-gate of the Footsteps.
Taking "as-it-is" as the wing and follower,
one abandons the seeking of the Dharma-gate;
taking the abandonment of seeking as the wing and follower.
This is the dharma-gate of abandoning all doubts and views;
taking this abandonment of all doubts and views as its wings and followers,
it is the dharma-gate of proceeding with equanimity.
Taking equal engagement as one's retinue;
taking the non-concealment of the Dharma-gates as one's retinue, by means of not concealing them.
The Dharma-gate of speech free from flattery;
taking speech free from flattery as one's retinue;
the Dharma-gate of not subduing others through the characteristics of speech.
Not using words to subdue one another is the support;
the dharma-gate of having no expectations is the support,
for having no expectations is the support.
The Dharma-gate of Non-Attachment,
which takes non-attachment as its winged retinue;
the Dharma-gate of Not Being Arrogant.
Taking non-lightheartedness as one's attendants;
taking the "unblinking" dharma-gate as one's attendants by means of being unblinking.

The step of sublime goodness, the step of traversing the furthest distance, the step of the mind free from desire, the step of movement, the step of no feet, the step of no mind, the step of laying down the burden, the step of composed composure, the step of enmity-free, the step of affliction-free, the step of Nirvāṇa, the step of suchness, the step of non-falling, the step of knowing and practicing, and the step of skillful guidance.

It is free from turbidity and impurity; free from delusion; free from arrogance; free from verbal expression; free from the thought of sorrow; free from the subduing of the weak by the strong; free from deficiency; free from inopportune timing; and free from lack of firmness.

If there are those who recite this dhāraṇī,

That person’s two hands are like mani jewels;

According to their needs for transformation and deliverance, all attained their aspirations;

He was also able to subdue non-Buddhist heretics and heterodox practitioners, such as the naked Nirgranthas, causing them all to enter the True Path.
His eloquence in responding to challenges was peerless in its artistry;

With a single word, he could respond to ten trillion voices.
Their deliberations were unerring.
They obtained the treasure of infinite talent, wisdom, and insight;
their fame spread everywhere, reaching throughout the immeasurable worlds of the ten directions.
They uphold all the teachings spoken by all Buddhas without forgetting them.
Having attained dharanis, they have reached a state entirely free from fear.
They understand and penetrate the nature of all phenomena as being like empty space.

He penetrates the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) as being like empty space.

They understand that the nature of the profound Dharma is like empty space,

Thus he overcomes his enemies.

If there is a person with a serious illness,

Whether it be a headache, a high fever, or ailments caused by wind, cold, or heat.

If there is further constant heat,

One should know that this is the supreme enemy:

Why is this? All Buddhas of the past have used these mantras to protect all sentient beings;
all Buddhas of the future shall likewise use these mantras to protect all sentient beings.
The Buddhas of the present also employ this mantra to protect all sentient beings.
You should know, O Victorious Foe,

It brings great benefit to immeasurable sentient beings.
As for this supreme enemy,
whoever recites this dhāraṇī sūtra and upholds it without forgetting, [shall attain such merit].
Eight billion yakṣas shall all provide protection for those who recite this dhāraṇī;

At that time, the yakṣa king Śvala was together with a host of sixty thousand yakṣas.
Approaching the place where the Buddha was, he knelt for a long time with palms joined and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One,
I shall lead my retinue to that place."
At that time, the yakṣa king Śvala addressed the Buddha again, saying: "World-Honored One, [you have promised] to protect those who recite this dhāraṇī."

All shall receive its grace and attain growth, with nothing failing to be accomplished.
I shall go into the Snowy Mountains to fetch the essence of the King of Medicines and bring it back day after day.

It causes those who recite and uphold this dhāraṇī to be forever free from all illnesses;

The Buddha again addressed Vijayavatī:

Those who protect, guard, and maintain the dhāraṇīs;
the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven who seek the Buddha-way;
and those of the Yāma Heaven, Tuṣita Heaven, Nirmāṇarati Heaven, and Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven who seek the Buddha-way.
Go to that place and all together protect and uphold the one who possesses the dhāraṇī;
that person shall enter the gate of the dhāraṇī of the seeds of the five aggregates.
Those of the five aggregates are called "without accomplishment";
they have no attachment or delight in this aggregate of form.
The earth element is called "earth";
the water element is called "water";
the fire element is called "fire."

Why is this? Because there is no established [substantiality], when one seeks its essential nature or even its name within the locus of earth, nothing at all can be found.
Because they lack intrinsic nature, there is nothing that is accomplished.
In this same way, the elements of water, fire,
and wind are likewise not accomplished.
Past form also does not say of itself, "I am past form.
Future form and present form are likewise so.

Why is this? Because the nature [of phenomena] is called equality, being a single state of non-conceptual knowledge.
Because they all return to emptiness.
If they lack intrinsic nature, then nothing can be accomplished.
This applies likewise to the nature of earth, water, fire, and wind.
Its nature is ineffable.
Past form is ineffable; as past form is ineffable, so too is this.
Future form is also beyond verbal expression, and present form is also beyond verbal expression. Why is this?
Because its nature is naturally ungraspable.
From what does it arise?
It arises from non-arising.
That which does not arise cannot cease.
Since there is nothing to be extinguished, there is no verbal teaching.
As it is said:
"The past, the future, and the present."
When one seeks the intrinsic nature of this aggregate of form, it is entirely unfindable.
How, then, could there be past, future, or present form?
For this reason, the same applies to the aggregates of sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
They are merely names and possess no solidity;
thus one enters the category of the five aggregates.
One also enters into dhāraṇī.
If one enters into dhāraṇī, then one enters into the five aggregates (skandhas).

Then one attains *dhāraṇī*.
Even that which is called the "seeking of *dhāraṇī*" cannot be apprehended;
therefore, it is merely a provisional designation.
Numbers are merely words;
idle chatter is merely words;
that which is spoken is merely words.

they do not enter into the category of form,
nor do they enter into dharani.
Nor can one attain the nature of dhāraṇī.
Why is this? Because in this matter, there is likewise no agent.
It is merely a word for "form" (rūpa). Furthermore,
because there is no inherent nature of the four great elements (mahābhūta) that can act as its creator,
one cannot find its accumulation.
Because there is nothing that accumulates, they are called the five aggregates (skandhas).
It is like a victorious enemy;
various matters gather together.
Up to the point where palaces and city walls are constructed,

A collection of various constituent factors is designated as "form"; yet,

The reason for this is that,
because their fundamental nature is extremely subtle, they cannot be apprehended. Why is this so?
The nature of the eye cannot be found by seeking it within the eye.
Why is this? Because it is fundamentally without intrinsic nature.
Because all phenomena are fundamentally without intrinsic nature, they cannot be apprehended.
If there is nothing to be apprehended, then there is nothing to be accomplished.
Since there is nothing to be accomplished, [there is no attainment].
Thus, there is neither arising nor ceasing.
Since there is no arising, there is no ceasing.
Since there is neither arising nor ceasing, there are no verbal designations for the past, the future, or the present.

numbers are merely characters.
Thus, within these characters, one cannot find the characters themselves.

The Buddha told Ānanda:
